scientific_question: Does the same-source Utah mule-deer minus bighorn observed GPS night/day displacement difference retain an association with fixed-43N astronomical daylight duration when slopes are centered within each already selected year×calendar-month block, rather than comparing across months?
published_study: Movebank Utah DOI 10.5441/001/1.711 (four native taxa, two explicitly fixed target taxa Odocoileus hemionus and Ovis canadensis)
source_sample: The EXACT 199 already qualified coobserved solar calendar days, 2 calendar years, 10 year×month blocks, fixed 43.0 degree-N astronomical reference, 10 original mule-deer tagged animals and 42 original bighorn tagged animals, and 2 fixed-point source eligibility iterations; no new year, taxon, schedule or date searching based on response sign.
source_provenance: Before any new month-conditioned calculation, verify original Movebank public original bitstream UUID, provider file bytes and MD5; replay all four Utah native source q and q~daylength means and original supported animal counts and both target taxa's original three UTC schedule tag-date effects to 1e−12. The original common-date q differences and original unadjusted slopes for each of 3 schedules must match frozen first source values to 1e−12.
same_calendar_design: Use previously fixed same-tag×year×date eligibility across original hourbin, even UTC 2h and odd UTC 2h, then existing Utah two-taxon iterative source coobserved-day intersection. Daywise response is the equal source tag mean on each qualifying date of q_mule - q_bighorn; q=NIGHT−DAY log1p straight-line original GPS step displacement speed, NOT active-time duration.
astronomical_exposure: Fixed 43.0 N computed daylight hours, exactly same as previous original Utah and Wyoming shared-calendar comparisons; not direct solar radiation, not actual animal local sun exposure.

month_conditioning.method: Preserve previous source code original per-year×calendar-month within-block centered OLS sxy/sxx from scripts/rsds_within_month_photoperiod_shared_calendar_v1.py, no variation of cutoffs.
month_conditioning.bootstrap: 2000 deterministic year×month-block bootstrap replicates, 2.5-97.5 percentile and leave-one-month-block-out range; descriptive nominal CI, no causal month-adjusted treatment effect.

measurements: For each ORIGINAL/EVEN/ODD schedule, report full archived all-month same-calendar pair slope and signed bootstrap status, strict numerical replay, eligible month blocks and days, pooled within-block daylength slope, month-block bootstrap95, leave-one-month-block-out range, and classification 'PERSISTS/NOT_RESOLVED' relative to original signed interval. Never impute zero for insufficiency.
original_4_study_macro_boundary: Four coobserved original field-study comparisons (Illinois, Wyoming, Utah, Geese) are not four independent native taxa. Existing source-only Utah month result is NOT_TESTED_WITHIN_MONTH_DO_NOT_INFER_ZERO; publish this as separate first result and later merge into comparative synthesis without modifying original source first result.
claim_ceiling: Post-outcome fixed-sample seasonal confounding diagnostic: a null-spanning month bootstrap does not prove absence of species difference.

Calendar month adjustment only removes between-month seasonal mean; daylight remains a deterministic function of date and can proxy temperature, forage, predators, weather and other within-month changes.
Source days are not independent tagged animals; 10 year-month blocks and two calendar years limit uncertainty and autocorrelation estimation.
Even and odd UTC schedules share tags/dates but use different source GPS displacement chords; the study is not a controlled animal chronotype experiment.
Only original Utah public field-study DOI, all four native source taxa preflight and two fixed comparison taxa, no new source selection or rescue.
No original GPS tagged individual IDs, exact dates/UTC times, locations, source private gridyears or per-tagged-animal effects are published.
